implementation_policy: Native PyBullet 3.2.5 rigid-body scene (CPU, dt=1/192000 s, 160 solver iterations, cone friction): a fixed 1.8 x 0.9 m tabletop at z=0, a 450 x 270 x 25 mm board on two 40 mm risers (top 65 mm), a free 74 x 64 x 50 mm, 145 g wooden block and a 2 mm push plate on a prismatic guide driven by a passive Hooke spring (steel wire 1.65 mm, coil 38 mm, 20 active turns, E=200 GPa, k=G d^4/(8 D^3 n) = 64.9 N/m, 75 mm precompression) with 0.12 N s/m viscous and 0.040 N dry guide friction; a fixed latch holds the plate until t=0.375 s, nothing is keyframed or launched. Board-block friction 0.22, table-block 0.24. States are saved at 240 Hz and at the 96 video instants t=i/24 s; a half-step run checks convergence (5 mm / 5 deg gates). Five edits change one parameter or object each (block mass x0.5, spring Young's modulus x0.25, table friction x0.5, delete the spring with its plate and moving guide, add a free 150 g block at rest on the table at the midpoint between a wooden bowl and a roll of tape, where the source block stops) and are audited by the shared edit DSL. Blender 4.3.2 Cycles replays the registered states (appearance/render.py + base_scene.py build the mechanism, block, board and table and key every body from the 240 Hz states; appearance/realism.py is the current look) at 1280x720 / 24 FPS / 96 frames from one fixed camera. tools/export_ground_truth.py writes per-frame ground truth from the native states and the camera; tools/publish_suite.py builds a suite in the current PCVE formats; --stage prompts / --export-prompts write the builder catalog prompts into the published suite.
